title: Snapshot-Pinned Batch Retrieval Contract
summary: Bounded search, context, and brief execution over one verified generated-index publication and one shared retrieval session.

release.compatibility: Shin v1.25 requires an explicit generator-v17 rebuild for corrected authority semantics. No compatibility reader or implicit migration is retained.

rules: unknown fields are rejected at both document and request level
request_id is required, bounded, non-control text, and unique within the document
query is required and must retain meaningful normalized terms
per_doc_limit is valid only for context and brief
the complete input and every expanded request are validated before the generated index lock is opened

session.lock: The CLI batch path holds one shared generated-index lock from session open through completion of every child retrieval. The candidate embedded immutable-snapshot path is a separate admission lifecycle defined in shin-warm-snapshot-v1, not an automatic daemon mode for this command.
session.freshness: Freshness is assessed once at session open. --require-current requires one exact current proof before child execution.
session.manifest: The active manifest is a non-symlink regular file, is bounded at 64 MiB, matches the session snapshot_id, and uses the supported KB schema and tool identity.
session.snapshotRule: The parent and every child result carry the same non-null snapshot_id.
session.parallelism: Independent requests may execute concurrently against immutable files under the same shared lock.
session.ordering: Result order always equals input request order regardless of worker scheduling.
session.outputBoundary: The complete bounded JSON document is built before the session and lock are destroyed; stdout emission happens after lock release.

resultEntry.resultRule: result is the unmodified structured result model of the requested search, context, or brief command, including evidence_kind and verification_level on evidence rows.

failurePolicy: The batch is atomic at the response level: invalid input or any child execution failure produces one shin.error.v1 document and no partial batch stdout.
No per-request retry or partial-success envelope is inferred by Core.
Resource ceilings fail before unbounded work or stdout emission.
verification: mixed search/context/brief result equivalence with standalone retrieval
one snapshot identity across parent and child results
serial and parallel result equality with stable input ordering
validation before index creation or lock acquisition
duplicate or control-byte id, unknown field, aggregate budget, request count, worker count, and input byte failures
